name: An Dinh Palace
kicker: Khai Dinh’s palace on the An Cuu
summary: Khải Định’s private palace on the An Cựu river, later the house of Crown Prince Vĩnh Thụy, the future Bảo Đại. Walk through the ceramic-relief gate and the octagonal Trung Lập pavilion to Khải Tường tower, a three-storey European-style castle with murals inside. Go for the late Nguyễn court in a European frame, a contrast to the Imperial City.
getThere: Phan Đình Phùng, on the An Cựu (no. 97 or no. 179 on the ticket record).
heroCaption: The yellow facade of Khải Tường tower at An Dinh

notice.title: A separate ticket
notice.body: The 200,000 VND Imperial City ticket does not include An Dinh. The palace has its own adult ticket, 50,000 VND, and children under 13 enter free.

body: An Dinh faces south on the An Cựu. Khải Định, then still Phụng Hóa Công, made a residence here in 1902 and rebuilt it with his own money from 1917 to early 1919. From 28 February 1922 it was the house of Crown Prince Vĩnh Thụy, later Bảo Đại. The family lived here after 1945. The grounds are 23,463 square metres.

Three buildings remain. The main gate is two storeys and three arches, with ceramic relief. Trung Lập, inside the gate, is an octagonal pavilion that held a life-size bronze of Khải Định cast in 1920. Khải Tường tower, behind it, is three storeys and 745 square metres, in the form of a European castle, with murals on the first floor.
An adult ticket is 50,000 VND, and children under 13 enter free. Hue residents and the other groups named in Resolution 55 pay half.

gettingThere: From the south bank, follow Phan Đình Phùng along the An Cựu river to the palace gate.
